rationale: Two real defects in the new default-tool checkbox routing: a silent no-op regression for ToolSelector/SkillForm consumers of ToolsConfiguration (CR-002, critical) and an invisible premature deselect when clicking an inactive default tool (CR-001, major). Exclusive-pair matching by label-text suffix is fragile with no safety net (CR-004, major), and the virtual-assistant save mapping for deselected_default_tools has no test coverage (CR-003, major). 5 findings dismissed as noise: the asymmetric filtering-variant resync reads as the spec's explicitly-allowed 'both deselected' state recoverable by one manual click; the watch('context') cast matches an existing pattern used elsewhere in the same file; the non-virtual-assistant AssistantTab branch spreads the existing actor config so any deselected_default_tools already present passes through unmodified; a cross-toolkit tool-name collision is implausible given the specific reserved names; and ExternalToolsSection never renders through Toolkit.tsx so default tools cannot reach that path. No defer findings — nothing here is pre-existing. All lenses and the standards audit ran and parsed cleanly; no decision_needed items remain.

findings.title: Default-tool checkbox silently deselects when inactive
findings.problem: The default-tool checkbox's onChange unconditionally calls toggleDefaultTool whenever tool.name matches a default tool, with no check that the tool is currently context-active; clicking an unchecked default-tool row when no matching datasource context is attached still records the tool in deselectedDefaultTools.
findings.impact: The checkbox stays visually unchecked before and after the click (isDefaultToolActive returns false regardless since context is absent), giving no feedback that anything changed; once a matching datasource is later attached, the tool silently fails to auto-select even though the author never knowingly deselected it, undermining the auto-select-unless-previously-deselected acceptance criterion.
findings.recommendation: Guard the onChange to no-op (or disable the checkbox) when the default tool is not currently context-active, so a click only ever toggles an already-active default tool.

findings.title: Default-tool routing breaks tool selection in other forms
findings.problem: The isDefaultToolName(tool.name) branch routes any tool with one of the three reserved names through toggleDefaultTool unconditionally, regardless of whether the hosting ToolsConfiguration consumer wired context/onDeselectedDefaultToolsChange. ToolSelector.tsx and SkillForm.tsx render ToolsConfiguration against the full internal toolkit catalog (now including get_repository_file_tree/search_code_repo in Codebase Tools) without passing context or onDeselectedDefaultToolsChange, so ToolsConfiguration's default onDeselectedDefaultToolsChange = () => {} absorbs the click.
findings.impact: Clicking the Get Repo Tree / Search Code checkbox in the script-tool picker or the Skill form's tool selection does nothing - no state change, no selection, no error - a silent regression of previously-working tool selection for any toolkit/tool carrying one of the three reserved default-tool names.
findings.recommendation: Scope the isDefaultToolName special-casing to only fire when toggleDefaultTool is backed by a real onDeselectedDefaultToolsChange, falling back to the normal toggleTool path otherwise, or restrict the default-tool branch to the two call sites (AssistantForm, VirtualAssistantForm) that pass context.

findings.title: No test for virtual-assistant default-tools save path
findings.problem: No test renders VirtualAssistantForm/AssistantTab and exercises handleDeselectedDefaultToolsChange, the getDefaultValues load of config?.deselected_default_tools, or the deselected_default_tools: virtualAssistantValues.deselected_default_tools ?? [] line in finalAssistantConfig; the only existing test calls the Yup schema directly and never touches the component or this save mapping.
findings.impact: If this line, or the default-values wiring it depends on, is ever dropped or reverted, workflow-editor virtual assistants would silently lose the deselect-default-tool feature on save/reload while the full existing test suite keeps passing.
findings.recommendation: Add a test that renders VirtualAssistantForm/AssistantTab, toggles a default tool off, saves, and asserts the resulting AssistantConfiguration.deselected_default_tools reflects the change, mirroring the existing AssistantForm.defaultTools.integration.test.tsx.

findings.title: Exclusive tool pairing matches by fragile label string
findings.problem: findExclusivePairTool pairs a default tool with its with-filtering variant purely by string-matching the user-facing label (suffix " with filtering"), with no shared constant or id-based relation tying the two tools together.
findings.impact: Any backend label wording change, added whitespace, or localization of either label silently breaks the pairing, so both the default tool and its with-filtering variant could end up selected simultaneously - violating the mutual-exclusivity guarantee the surrounding code asserts - with no compile-time or runtime signal that the pairing broke.
findings.recommendation: Correlate the pair by a stable identifier (a tool id/relation field from the backend) rather than label text, or at minimum centralize both label strings in one shared constant with a test asserting the pairing resolves for every known default tool.
